source: City of Portland, Oregon: Heritage Trees (Bureau of Parks and Recreation, Heritage Tree ordinance)
licence_proof: Item metadata field licenseInfo = "CC-BY-SA" on https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/content/items/db48b717d0174906b95f028c83c09dd0?f=json, surfaced via the gis-pdx.opendata.arcgis.com dataset page. Note the ShareAlike clause: unlike a plain CC BY register, derivative datasets built from this one would themselves need to carry a compatible open licence if redistributed as a dataset. Using the facts (species, coordinates) to write an original story is not redistributing their dataset, but a bulk re-export of this file should stay attributed and open.
designation: Heritage Tree (City of Portland ordinance, Portland City Code ch. 20 / Title 11): trees added annually by the City Forester for age, size, type, historical association or horticultural value. A real semantic designation, not a street-tree inventory.
attribution: City of Portland, Bureau of Parks and Recreation
scope: All 463 records in the live feed, filtered here to the 429 never delisted. The 34 delisted entries are recorded separately below under blocked_delisted, never imported as live trees.
vitality_field: Delist_Date / Delist_Ordinance / Delist_Reason exist and are populated for 34 of 463 trees (removed, hazard, dead, owner request, etc). This is unusually good for a register: most carry no vitality signal at all. A populated Delist_Date is being treated as a hard block, per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's 'a tree you KNOW is dead is never delivered.' An empty Delist_Date is NOT proof of life on its own (last_edited_date on most rows is old); still treat 'currently listed, not delisted' as one supporting signal, not a substitute for the normal alive-now check.
caveat: Three things a run must know. (1) Units are not labelled on the service: HEIGHT and SPREAD read as feet, DIAMETER reads as inches (standard US arboriculture DBH-in-inches), CIRCUMF reads as feet; this is inferred from internal consistency (e.g. a 25-inch diameter trunk implies a ~6.5 ft circumference, close to the 7.6 ft recorded) and not from an explicit units field, so treat these as likely-feet/likely-inches, not certain. (2) Ownership varies: many are 'Right Of Way' (public), many are 'Private, Front Yard' or similar; hard rule 10 applies per tree; do not publish a private-yard heritage tree as visitable without checking street visibility. (3) YEAR_Designated / DATE_DESIG give when the city recognised the tree, not the tree's age; age is not a field in this register at all and must come from elsewhere.
verdict: USABLE, imported (facts only, private-yard ownership must be filtered per hard rule 10 before any tree ships)

rule10_note: Hard rule 10 filter, added on import 2026-08-13. Portland's Heritage Tree ordinance protects trees on PRIVATE ground as readily as public: 169 of 429 sit in front, side or rear yards, and a rear-yard tree cannot be visited or even seen. Only rows marked rule10=public may be considered for publication; 'unknown' (44 rows with no ownership value) must be checked per tree before it ships, never assumed. This is the field that decides whether a register is usable at all, and it is why the survey's own rule is to look for ownership and vitality before anything else.
